
6p-Block Double-Zeta Basis Set Archive
======================================


Date: 23 Jun 2006


When publishing work that uses these basis sets, please use the following citation:

K.G. Dyall, Theor. Chem. Acc. (1998) 99:366; addendum Theor. Chem. Acc. (2002) 108:365; 
revision Theor. Chem. Acc. (2006) 115:441. Basis sets available from the Dirac web site, 
http://dirac.chem.sdu.dk.



This archive contains the exponents and the SCF spinor or orbital coefficients,
given with respect to normalized (spherical or 2-spinor) Gaussian functions, for
the basis sets described in the above articles. The SCF exponent sets reported
include the valence correlating functions. The d sets were reoptimized after
addition of the valence correlating d function, which was held fixed. The
outermost exponent of the f set was replaced by the core correlating f exponet
and the remaining f exponents reoptimized. In all the following descriptions,
this is the set referred to as the SCF exponent set.

The archive is set out as follows.

1. Exponents and SCF coefficients for Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave functions, in
   order of Z. The large component functions are given first, followed by the
   small component functions. Both components are labelled with the large
   component symmetry type, but the primitive functions for the small component
   are those obtained by restricted kinetic balance from the large component.  
   The spin-orbit components are labeled with "-" for j=l-1/2 and "+" for j=l+1/2.   

2. Exponents and SCF coefficients for spin-free modified Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave
   functions, in order of Z. The large component functions are given first, 
   followed by the pseudo-large component functions, then the Foldy-Wouthuysen
   transformed large component functions. Note that all components have the same
   symmetry type. 

3. Exponents of diffuse s, p, and d functions.

4. Exponents of valence and core correlating functions.

5. Exponents of core polarizing functions.



Basis set construction.
----------------------

Several different types of basis sets may be constructed by adding primitive
functions. These basis sets are described below.

NOTE: Functions are counted from the function with the smallest exponent to the largest. 

1. Valence (equivalent to cc-pvdz). To the SCF occupied set, add the following:
   1st s primitive from the SCF set 
   1st p primitive from the SCF set
   1st d primitive from the SCF set (correlating d)

   (HF + 1s1p1d valence)

2. Core-valence. To basis set 1, add the following:
   3rd s primitive from the SCF set 
   3rd p primitive from the SCF set
   2nd d primitive from the SCF set 
   1st f primitive from the SCF set (correlating f)

   (HF + 1s1p1d valence + 1s1p1d1f core)

3. Dipole polarization of the (n-1)d shell. To basis set 2, add the polarizing
   f exponent.

   (HF + 1s1p1d valence + 1s1p1d2f core)

4. Diffuse basis: add the diffuse s, p and d functions to any of the above
   basis sets.





Dirac-Hartree-Fock basis sets           
=============================
